Leak 1 · Invisible on Google

Too few reviews. Customers pick the other guy.

47% of customers won't even consider a business under 20 reviews — and 97% read reviews before choosing. An unfinished profile buries you before price or quality comes up.

The fix: profile completed and corrected, photos refreshed, review requests sent the same day every job finishes, and a reply drafted to every review.

"Getting consistent Google reviews has been tougher than expected."

— Small-business owner, r/smallbusiness via Out of the Box SEO. The theme from owners: happy customers never review — nobody asks.

Leak 2 · The phone rings out

Missed calls. The caller just dials your competitor.

~62% of small-business calls go unanswered. ~80% of callers who hit voicemail hang up without a message. The average business takes 42 hours to answer a web lead.

The fix: every missed call gets a text in under 30 seconds. Every web lead gets one in under 5 minutes — then 5 follow-ups over 5 days, automatically.

A landscaping owner measured it himself: 58% of his calls were missed — roughly $9–10k a week leaking. "The caller moves on to the next landscaper on Google."

— Owner's own account, DEV Community

Leak 3 · The empty chair

Booked. Then they never show.

~23% of appointments no-show. Each empty slot is worth ~$200 — one a day models to $20,000–$70,000 a year. Owners complain about this louder than almost anything else.

The fix: online booking, automatic reminders, one-tap reschedule, and a same-day text that offers any freed slot to your waitlist.

What each layer is worth, honestly

  • Reminders — the proven layer. −28.9% no-shows across 29 studies. On your 44 lost slots: ~13 back, ≈ $2,500/month.
  • Easy reschedule — the leak-stopper. Many "no-shows" meant to move the appointment. One tap turns a lost slot into a moved one.
  • Card-on-file + waitlist backfill — the recovery layer. Reminders alone don't solve it; owners in the research added these next. No published percentage exists — we claim none.

Sample business and schedule are illustrative; no patient information is involved. Statistics: no-show average via TRTC / Journal of General Internal Medicine, 2026; $200 per missed appointment, SCI Solutions/MGMA via Curogram; ADA HPI via Dental Signal, 2026; reminder reduction, Hasvold & Wootton via AIToolDaily, 2026. Zenoti's 2025 benchmark of salons already on booking software found ~3% no-shows vs ~20% in other compilations — a disagreement we note rather than hide (Zilo).

Two famous numbers you will not hear from us

  • "85% of missed callers never call back." No traceable primary source — every citation points at another blog. (SaveMyCalls audit, 2026)
  • "Businesses waste 26% of ad spend." Published figures run 8.5%–25% depending on definition. No single honest number exists — so we quote none.
